**re: How many match edges of each relation — exact, close, broad, narrow — does the graph hold, and what share of the non-hub properties is mapped?** Here is the full picture from the live graph: --- ### Match-Edge Counts by Relation | Relation | Edge Count | Share of Total | |---|---|---| | **CLOSE_MATCH** | 7,822 | ~40% | | **BROAD_MATCH** | 4,565 | ~23% | | **EXACT_MATCH** | 4,501 | ~23% | | **NARROW_MATCH** | 2,634 | ~13% | | **Total** | **19,522** | — | A few interpretive notes: - **CLOSE_MATCH is the plurality** — nearly as many edges say "near but not interchangeable" as EXACT and BROAD combined. This reflects the practical reality that natural-language alignment rarely lands on perfect synonymy. - **EXACT_MATCH and BROAD_MATCH are nearly equal** — together they represent the "confident" half of the corpus (exact synonymy vs. the hub concept being wider than the source element). - **NARROW_MATCH** (hub concept narrower than the source element) is the least common — expected, since hub ontologies tend to be broad reference frameworks. - All four are judgments, not established facts. Each edge carries a `mappingConfidence`, `mappingKind`, and `mappingSource` recording who decided and how sure they were. --- ### Non-Hub Property Mapping Coverage | Metric | Value | |---|---| | Total non-hub properties | 17,891 | | Mapped properties (any relation) | 6,591 | | **Coverage rate** | **36.84%** | | Hub properties excluded (CEDS + CTDL) | 2,721 | - The two hub standards — **CEDS** and **CTDL** — are excluded from this denominator (they do not map to themselves). - Of the 6,591 mapped properties: **5,866** reach a CEDS hub concept, and **2,202** reach a CTDL hub concept (some properties map to both). - That leaves roughly **11,300 non-hub properties currently unmapped** — the annotation backlog.
